description: The bar chart, titled "Factual Errors," compares the number of factual errors across four different question-answering systems—HotpotQA, 2WikiMQA, MuSiQue, and IIRC—under three distinct configurations: NoR QA, OneR QA, and IRCoT QA. The horizontal axis lists the four datasets, while the vertical axis represents the count of factual errors, scaled from 0 to 40. For each dataset, three bars are displayed side-by-side, representing the error counts for the respective QA configurations. The bars are color-coded and labeled in the legend: yellow with a dot pattern for NoR QA, red with a dot pattern for OneR QA, and blue with a diagonal line pattern for IRCoT QA. The data shows that the IRCoT QA configuration consistently results in the lowest number of factual errors across all four datasets. For instance, in the 2WikiMQA dataset, the error count drops from 29 (NoR QA) to 23 (OneR QA) and then to 14 (IRCoT QA). Similarly, in the MuSiQue dataset, the errors decrease from 28 to 27 and then to 23. The IIRC dataset shows a similar trend, with errors decreasing from 15 to 14 and then to 11. The HotpotQA dataset also shows a reduction from 15 to 10 and then to 5. This indicates that the IRCoT QA method is effective in reducing factual errors compared to the other two methods.
